subject: Theory of Machines
summary: Displacement, velocity and acceleration analysis of plane mechanisms (four-bar, slider-crank, quick-return), Grashof's law and inversions, instantaneous centres and Kennedy's theorem, and the Coriolis component

questions.text: A four-bar chain ABCD has AB = 25 mm, BC = 60 mm, CD = 45 mm and DA = 55 mm. To obtain a double-rocker mechanism, the link to be fixed is
solution: Concept: Grashof's law: if s + l ≤ p + q, at least one link can rotate fully. Which link is fixed then decides the type.
s + l = 25 + 60 = 85; p + q = 45 + 55 = 100. 85 < 100, so the chain is Grashof.
Fix a link adjacent to the shortest link (BC or DA) → crank-rocker. Fix the shortest link AB → double-crank. Fix the link opposite the shortest (CD) → double-rocker.
Exam tip: In a Grashof chain the shortest link is the only one that can rotate fully. Find it first, then read off the type from where the fixed link sits relative to it.

questions.text: A planar mechanism has 8 links (including the frame), 10 binary turning pairs and 1 higher pair (cam contact). Its degree of freedom by the Kutzbach criterion is ______
solution: Concept: Kutzbach (planar): F = 3(n − 1) − 2j − h, where j = lower pairs and h = higher pairs.
F = 0 means the assembly is a structure: no relative motion is possible.
Exam tip: F = 1 is a constrained mechanism, F = 0 a structure, F < 0 a statically indeterminate (superstructure). Count each ternary joint as two binary joints.

questions.text: A planar mechanism has a total of 28 instantaneous centres. The number of links in it (including the frame) is
solution: Concept: With n links there are N = n(n − 1)/2 instantaneous centres, one for each pair of links.
Exam tip: 56 is n(n − 1), not n. Primary ICs are found by inspection (pins, sliders, rolling contacts); the rest come from Kennedy's theorem.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT an inversion of the double slider-crank chain?
solution: Concept: The double slider-crank chain has two turning pairs and two sliding pairs. Its three inversions are the elliptical trammel, the Scotch yoke and Oldham's coupling.
The Whitworth quick-return mechanism comes from the single slider-crank chain, by fixing the crank.
Exam tip: Single slider-crank inversions: engine (frame fixed), Whitworth / rotary engine (crank fixed), oscillating cylinder / slotted lever (connecting rod fixed), hand pump (slider fixed).

questions.text: In the slider-crank mechanism shown, crank OA = 60 mm rotates at 50 rad/s and the connecting rod AP = 240 mm. When the crank is at 120° from the inner dead centre, the velocity of the slider P (in m/s) is ______
solution: Concept: Exact slider-crank velocity: vP = ωr sin(θ + φ)/cos φ, where sin φ = (r/l) sin θ.
Exam tip: The approximate form ωr(sin θ + sin 2θ/2n) gives 3.0 × (0.866 − 0.108) = 2.27 m/s here too. For 90° < θ < 180° the sin 2θ term is negative, so the slider is slower than ωr sin θ.

questions.text: In a slider-crank mechanism the crank is 100 mm, the connecting rod 500 mm and the crank turns uniformly at 40 rad/s. At the inner dead centre, the angular velocity of the connecting rod is
solution: Concept: ωAP = ω cos θ/√(n² − sin²θ), where n = l/r.
At θ = 0: ωAP = ω/n = 40/5 = 8 rad/s
Equivalently, v<sub>A</sub> = 40 × 0.1 = 4 m/s is perpendicular to the rod, and the slider is momentarily at rest, so ω<sub>AP</sub> = 4/0.5 = 8 rad/s.
Exam tip: The rod's angular velocity is greatest at the dead centres (ω/n) and zero at θ = 90°. Don't mix this up with its angular acceleration, which is zero at the dead centres.

questions.text: In the four-bar mechanism shown (dimensions in mm), the crank O<sub>2</sub>A rotates at 15 rad/s counter-clockwise. Using the instantaneous centre method, the angular velocity of the rocker O<sub>4</sub>B (in rad/s) at this position is ______
solution: Concept: The IC of the coupler (I13) lies where the line O2A extended meets the line O4B extended. Every point of AB moves as if rotating about it.
Coordinates (O<sub>2</sub> at the origin): A = (28.28, 28.28), B = (108.29, 69.51), O<sub>4</sub> = (100, 0)
Line O2A (y = x) meets line O4B at I13 = (113.54, 113.54), so IA = 120.57 mm and IB = 44.34 mm
Exam tip: Short cut: ω4/ω2 = (O2A/IA) × (IB/O4B). Always sketch the IC; it shows at a glance whether the answer is sensible.

questions.text: A slider moves radially outward along a link that rotates clockwise at constant speed. The Coriolis component of the slider's acceleration is directed
opts: perpendicular to the link, obtained by rotating the outward sliding velocity 90° clockwise
perpendicular to the link, obtained by rotating the outward sliding velocity 90° counter-clockwise
along the link, toward the centre of rotation
questions.ans: (A) perpendicular to the link, obtained by rotating the outward sliding velocity 90° clockwise
solution: Concept: Coriolis acceleration = 2ω × vrel. Its magnitude is 2ωv and it is always perpendicular to the link.
Direction: rotate the relative (sliding) velocity vector through 90° in the same sense as ω.
ω is clockwise and v<sub>rel</sub> is outward, so rotate the outward direction 90° clockwise.
Exam tip: The centripetal term (rω², toward the centre) acts along the link. The Coriolis term never does.

questions.text: In a crank and slotted-lever quick-return mechanism, the distance between the fixed centres is 240 mm. For the ratio of the cutting-stroke time to the return-stroke time to be 1.5, the length of the crank (in mm) must be ______
solution: Concept: At the two extreme positions the slotted lever is tangent to the crank circle, so the crank is perpendicular to the lever. If β is the crank angle for the return stroke, cos(β/2) = r/d.
Exam tip: The time ratio depends only on r/d. The lever length changes only the stroke length (2L·r/d).

questions.text: A horizontal engine has a 75 mm crank and a 375 mm connecting rod, and runs at 900 rpm. The magnitude of the piston's acceleration at the outer dead centre (in m/s²) is ______
solution: Concept: Piston acceleration a = ω²r(cos θ + cos 2θ/n). At the dead centres this is exact: ω²r(1 + 1/n) at the IDC and ω²r(1 − 1/n) at the ODC.
Exam tip: The IDC value is larger: 8882.6 × 0.075 × 1.2 = 799.4 m/s². That is why the maximum inertia force acts at the inner dead centre.

questions.text: In the four-bar mechanism shown, O<sub>2</sub> is at the origin, A is at (30, 40) mm, B is at (130, 40) mm and O<sub>4</sub> is at (130, −60) mm. The crank O<sub>2</sub>A rotates counter-clockwise at a uniform 10 rad/s. The magnitude of the angular acceleration of the rocker O<sub>4</sub>B (in rad/s²) is ______
solution: Concept: Velocity first, then acceleration: aB = aA + α3 × AB − ω3²AB, and aB = α4 × O4B − ω4²O4B.
Velocity: vA = 10k × (30, 40) = (−400, 300) mm/s. vB is horizontal (O4B is vertical), and AB is horizontal, so 300 + 100ω3 = 0 → ω3 = −3 rad/s (cw). Then vB = (−400, 0) = −100ω4 → ω4 = 4 rad/s (ccw).
From the rocker: a<sub>B</sub> = α<sub>4</sub>k × (0, 100) − 16(0, 100) = (−100α<sub>4</sub>, −1600)
x-components: −100α4 = −3900 → α4 = 39 rad/s² (ccw); y-components give α3 = 24 rad/s².
Exam tip: Choose components that kill unknowns. Here the rocker is vertical, so the x-equation contains only α4. Never drop the centripetal terms (ω²r) in an acceleration polygon.

questions.text: A crank-rocker mechanism has crank 30 mm, coupler 90 mm, rocker 80 mm and fixed link 100 mm. The minimum transmission angle during a revolution of the crank is nearly
solution: Concept: Transmission angle μ = angle between the coupler and the rocker: cos μ = (b² + c² − BD²)/(2bc), where BD is the distance from the crank pin to the rocker pivot.
BD is smallest when the crank lies along the fixed link towards O4: BD = 100 − 30 = 70 mm
When the crank points away from O<sub>4</sub>, BD = 130 mm and μ<sub>max</sub> = 99.6°.
Exam tip: Good designs keep μ between about 40° and 140°. The extremes always occur with the crank collinear with the fixed link.

questions.text: In the crank and slotted-lever mechanism shown, the crank O<sub>2</sub>A = 80 mm rotates counter-clockwise at 25 rad/s, and the lever pivot O<sub>1</sub> is 200 mm vertically below O<sub>2</sub>. When the crank is 30° above the horizontal, the angular velocity of the slotted lever (in rad/s) is ______
solution: Concept: The velocity of the crank pin A splits into a component along the lever (sliding velocity) and a component across it, which turns the lever: ωlever = v⊥/O1A.
A = (80 cos 30°, 200 + 80 sin 30°) = (69.28, 240) mm → O1A = 249.8 mm; unit vector along the lever u = (0.2774, 0.9608)
ωlever = 1441.2/249.8 = 5.77 rad/s; the sliding velocity is vA · u = 1386.8 mm/s
Exam tip: Both components are needed for the Coriolis term 2ωlevervs (here 2 × 5.77 × 1.387 = 16.0 m/s²).

questions.text: In the offset slider-crank mechanism shown, crank r = 50 mm, connecting rod l = 150 mm and the line of stroke is offset by e = 60 mm from the crank centre. The stroke of the slider is nearly
solution: Concept: The extreme slider positions occur when the crank and connecting rod are collinear: extended (distance l + r from O) and folded (l − r).
Exam tip: With an offset the stroke exceeds 2r and the two strokes take unequal crank angles, so the mechanism also gives a quick return.

questions.text: A slider-crank mechanism has crank OA = 50 mm and connecting rod AP = 200 mm. The crank rotates at 20 rad/s. When the crank is at 45° from the inner dead centre, the speed of the midpoint M of the connecting rod (in m/s) is ______ (round off to 3 decimal places)
solution: Concept: The IC of the connecting rod (I) lies where line OA extended meets the vertical through P (the perpendicular to the slider's velocity). Every point's speed is ωAP × its distance from I.
Exam tip: The slider's speed is vP = ωAP × IP = 3.592 × 232.21 = 0.834 m/s. A coupler point's speed is not the average of the speeds of its ends.
